messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Copy feature beta to beta_season
parts:
Dear INLA experts,


I am developing a joint model: 

y ~ y.b0 + sy.0 + sy.1

z ~ z.b0 + beta * (sy.0 + sy.1)


where sy.0 is time-constant spatial field, and sy.1 is monthly-specific spatial field.


The model formula is:

form <- y ~ -1 + y.b0 + e.b0 +

  f(sy.0, model=spde) +

  f(sy.1, model=spde, group=sy.1.group, control.group=list(model="ar1", hyper=rho_cp, scale.model=TRUE)) +

  

  f(sz.0, copy="sy.0",  fixed=FALSE, hyper=hypercopy) + 

  f(sz.1, copy="sy.1", same.as="sz.0", group=sey.1.group, fixed=FALSE, hyper=hypercopy)


I want to extend beta to beta_season, meaning beta_season will vary across different seasons. Is this possible?


Thanks,

Ruby

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Copy feature beta to beta_season
parts:
if you have two seasons, you can have two copies but only one of them are
observed,

like

y ~ f(x)
yy ~ beta.1 * f(x) + beta.2 * f(x)

then you let the index of the first copy be 1 if its season 1 and NA if its in
season 2. and the oposiste for copy 2

messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Copy feature beta to beta_season
parts:
Thank you for the advice. I’m not sure how to set beta.1 to 1 if it’s season 1 and NA if it’s season 2 in INLA.

I am considering defining u = f(x), then using f(e.season1, copy="u") + f(e.season2, copy="u"). Here, e.season1 is 1 when it’s season 1 and NA when it’s season 2, and the opposite for e.season2.

I’m not sure if this approach will achieve my goal, and I’m hesitant to add a linear predictor on u, as it might significantly increase computation time.

Thanks,
Rujia
